items.title: [fix]: prevent unsafe MCP tool-call replay
items.body:
Summary

Prevent automatic MCP retries from duplicating non-idempotent operations after an ambiguous failure.

A local reproduction committed a mutation, lost its response, and then committed it again when Bifrost retried. The ordinary retry path did not check tool annotations; recovery also allowed additive, non-idempotent tools through its safety gate.

Changes

  • Apply a shared replay-safety check to ordinary retries and authentication/session recovery.
  • Require an explicit read-only or idempotent hint; missing hints and destructiveHint=false alone do not authorize replay.
  • Recheck eligibility before repeated invocations and after connection healing.
  • Preserve credential refresh and connection repair without replaying unsafe operations.
  • Exclude tool-domain errors from ordinary transport retry classification and match HTTP statuses in status position.
  • Report that execution may have succeeded when automatic replay is suppressed.
  • Add real local-server regressions, classification tests, and a successful-call benchmark.
  • Document annotation trust requirements and ambiguous-outcome handling.

Code Mode retains its separate, single-invocation execution path. No temporary artifacts or standalone example-fixture changes remain in the final diff.

Type of change

  • [x] Bug fix
  • [ ] Feature
  • [ ] Refactor
  • [x] Documentation
  • [ ] Chore/CI

Affected areas

  • [x] Core (Go)
  • [x] Transports (HTTP)
  • [ ] Providers/Integrations
  • [ ] Plugins
  • [ ] UI (React)
  • [x] Docs

How to test

From the repository root:

cd core

GOWORK=off GOTOOLCHAIN=go1.27.3 go test ./mcp ./mcp/codemode/starlark -count=1

GOWORK=off GOTOOLCHAIN=go1.27.3 go test ./mcp ./mcp/codemode/starlark \
  -run '^TestMCPToolReplaySafety_|^TestIsTransientToolCallError|^TestToolCallReplayAllowed' \
  -count=20

GOWORK=off GOTOOLCHAIN=go1.27.3 go test -race ./mcp ./mcp/codemode/starlark \
  -run '^TestMCPToolReplaySafety_|^TestExecuteTool_AuthFailureRetry_|^TestIsTransientToolCallError|^TestToolCallReplayAllowed' \
  -count=1

GOWORK=off GOTOOLCHAIN=go1.27.3 go test ./mcp -run '^$' \
  -bench '^BenchmarkMCPToolExecutionReplayPolicy$' -benchmem

Expected outcomes:

  • Unknown, destructive, and additive non-idempotent operations commit once after response loss.
  • Genuine idempotent controls commit once despite repeated invocations; read-only controls do not mutate.
  • Cancellation, deadline expiry, and revoked eligibility during backoff prevent another invocation.
  • Direct and agent-generated calls sharing the executor have consistent behavior.

Validation passed: full MCP/Code Mode packages, race checks, and 72 local-server scenarios repeated 20 times. Real Chat/Responses HTTP checks also confirmed one commit per unsafe logical call.

No paid provider harness, full provider suite, UI build, or complete CI pipeline was run.

Request-path cost

Five alternating before/after samples of successful in-process execution:

Contract | Before ns/op | After ns/op | Allocations before/after -- | -- | -- | -- Unannotated | 15,447 | 14,165 | 89 / 89 Read-only | 13,671 | 13,912 | 89 / 89 Idempotent | 13,191 | 14,351 | 89 / 89

Timing varies; no blanket latency improvement is claimed. Allocation counts are unchanged. Policy lookup is failure-only, existing manager state is reused, and no retained cache or request-content storage is added.

No new configuration fields or environment variables are introduced.

Screenshots/Recordings

Not applicable; no UI changes.

Breaking changes

  • [x] Yes
  • [ ] No

Retry behavior changes intentionally: tools without an explicit replay-safe hint no longer receive automatic replay after qualifying failures. Public method signatures and configuration schemas are unchanged.

Only opt genuinely read-only or idempotent operations into retries, using annotations from trusted servers. Do not mark an unsafe operation idempotent merely to restore availability.

Related issues

Related implementation work: #5911, #5713, #5726, and #6923.

Closes #8795

Security considerations

Reduces duplicate-mutation risk without changing tool permissions or credential isolation.

Annotations remain advisory and are not independently verified. Incorrect server hints can still permit duplicate effects; this change does not guarantee exactly-once execution. An execution failure or cancellation does not imply that an upstream mutation was rolled back.

Checklist

  • [ ] I read docs/contributing/README.md and followed the guidelines
  • [x] I added/updated tests where appropriate
  • [x] I updated documentation where needed
  • [ ] I verified builds succeed (Go and UI)
  • [ ] I verified the CI pipeline passes locally if applicable

items.title: [Bug]: Replayed Responses reasoning item IDs can be non-replayable across turns
items.body:
### Prerequisites

- [x] I searched existing issues and pull requests for duplicates.
- [x] I reproduced the behavior on the current `dev` branch.

### Description

Some OpenAI-compatible Responses providers return reasoning items with both `encrypted_content` and a server-side item `id`, but the `id` cannot be resolved when the client replays the item on a later turn. The upstream rejects the second request even though stateless replay through `encrypted_content` remains valid.

This was reproduced with Prime using a Responses-compatible OpenCode Go endpoint: the first turn returned a reasoning item and a tool call; the second turn replayed the reasoning item and failed with a 400.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Send a Responses request with `store:false` to a provider that returns a reasoning item containing `id` and `encrypted_content`.
2. Execute the returned tool call.
3. Replay the complete reasoning item alongside the tool result in the next request.
4. Observe the provider reject the reasoning item ID.

Protocol probes showed:

- replaying `id` plus `encrypted_content`: 400
- replaying the same item after removing only `id`: 200
- changing to `store:true`: still 400

### Expected behavior

When the upstream specifically reports that a referenced reasoning item was not found or expired, Bifrost should retry once on the same key after removing only the reasoning item IDs. It should preserve `encrypted_content`, summaries, and unrelated input fields.

### Actual behavior

Bifrost returns the upstream 400 directly, terminating otherwise valid multi-turn tool use.

### Affected area(s)

Core (Go)

### Version

Reproduced on `transports/v1.6.11`; the current `dev` branch (`0ac7f7142`) does not handle this error variant.

### Environment

```text
Client: Prime 0.7.1
API: Responses, multi-turn tool call
Provider shape: OpenAI-compatible Responses
Observed error: Referenced reasoning item ... was not found or has expired
```

### Severity

High (major functionality broken)

items.title: [fix]: Anthropic provider - keep a deferred web search pending on replay
items.body:
## Summary

Fixes #9591. When Claude calls a client tool and `web_search` in the same turn, Anthropic defers the search: the turn ends with `stop_reason: "tool_use"` and a `server_tool_use` that has no `web_search_tool_result`. The client sends that turn back with the client `tool_result` blocks, and Anthropic then runs the search.

Bifrost rebuilt that turn with a `web_search_tool_result` after every web search `server_tool_use`. The pending search reached Anthropic as a finished one placed after the client `tool_use`, and the request was rejected:

```
400 invalid_request_error
`tool_use` ids were found without `tool_result` blocks immediately after: toolu_…
```

The non-streaming response had the same problem in the other direction: the client received an empty `web_search_tool_result` for a search that had not run.

## Changes

- **Ingress** (`convertAnthropicContentBlocksToResponsesMessagesOrdered`): a web search `server_tool_use` becomes a `web_search_call` with status `in_progress`. `attachWebSearchSourcesToCall` sets it to `completed` when the result block arrives. It was `completed` from the start, so a pending search and a finished one with no hits looked the same.
- **Egress** (`convertBifrostWebSearchCallToAnthropicBlocks`): an `in_progress` call is rebuilt as a bare `server_tool_use`. Every other status, and no status, still gets the result block, so history from providers that do not replay one (OpenAI, Gemini) is unchanged.

Two things already in the code make this the consistent choice. The streaming path gives a search with no result yet the status `in_progress` and only emits `completed` when the result block ends. And `convertBifrostWebFetchCallToAnthropicBlocks` already returns a bare `server_tool_use` when a fetch has no result.

Wire-visible change on `/v1/responses`: in a non-streaming response, a search Anthropic deferred is now reported as `in_progress`, not `completed`.

### Routes

| Route | Covered | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `/anthropic/v1/messages` request | Yes | Unit tests and harness pair |
| `/anthropic/v1/messages` non-streaming response | Yes | Unit test and harness turn 1 |
| `/v1/responses` and the Go SDK | Yes | Unit tests and harness pair. The pending search is an `in_progress` `web_search_call`, and it survives the JSON round trip |
| Vertex, Azure | Yes | Same converters through `BuildAnthropicResponsesRequestBody`. Unit tests run the request path with `vertex/` and `azure/` models |
| Streaming response | Not changed | It already reports the search as `in_progress` |
| `/v1/chat/completions` | Not reached | The chat wire has no item for a server tool call in history |
| Bedrock | Not reached | Bedrock uses the grouped ingress and its own egress (`web_search_call` becomes Nova grounding). Neither is touched |

### Not covered

When the continuation succeeds, Anthropic returns the `web_search_tool_result` at the start of the next assistant message, apart from its `server_tool_use`. Bifrost drops a result block whose call is not in the same message, on the non-streaming response, in the stream ("If no matching tool ID, skip") and on request replay. That is existing behavior and needs a neutral shape for a result that arrives in a later message, so I left it out of this fix. I can open a separate issue for it.

## Type of change

- [x] Bug fix
- [ ] Feature
- [ ] Refactor
- [ ] Documentation
- [ ] Chore/CI

## Affected areas

- [x] Core (Go)
- [ ] Transports (HTTP)
- [x] Providers/Integrations
- [ ] Plugins
- [ ] UI (React)
- [ ] Docs

## How to test

Unit tests, added to `core/providers/anthropic/websearch_test.go`. The three pending-search tests failed before the fix on the extra `web_search_tool_result` and on status `completed`; the finished-search test passed before and after.

- `TestWebSearch_PendingCallKeepsNoResultOnRequestRoundTrip`: client tool before the search, search before the client tool, and a paused turn, for the bare, `anthropic/`, `vertex/` and `azure/` model forms.
- `TestWebSearch_FinishedCallKeepsResultOnRequestRoundTrip`: a search with sources, with no sources, and with an error result all keep their result block.
- `TestWebSearch_NeutralCallStatusDecidesResultBlock`: only `in_progress` is sent bare; `completed`, `failed` and no status still get the result block.
- `TestWebSearch_PendingCallKeepsNoResultOnResponse`: non-streaming response on both routes, then the `/v1/responses` output replayed through JSON.

```sh
cd core
go test ./providers/anthropic/ -run 'TestWebSearch_' -count=1
go test ./providers/anthropic/ ./providers/vertex/ ./providers/azure/ ./providers/bedrock/ ./providers/openai/ ./schemas/ -count=1
```

Also green: `transports/bifrost-http/integrations` and `framework/tracing`.

Provider harness: folder `310. Anthropic deferred web search continuation (#9591) (deferred web search)`, four cases in two chains (`/anthropic/v1/messages` and `/v1/responses`). Turn 1 asks for both calls in one reply and saves the output. Turn 2 sends it back and asserts a 200 plus, through `raw_request`, that the upstream body carries the pending `server_tool_use` and no `web_search_tool_result` for it. Validated with `augment-provider-harness.mjs` and `filter-collection.mjs` (4 requests kept for `--provider anthropic --feature "deferred web search"`). The collection diff is additions only.

**Not run:** the live harness and `make test-core PROVIDER=anthropic`. I have no provider keys in this environment, so the fix is not yet proven against the live API. Turn 1 depends on the model issuing both calls in one turn.

```bash
docker compose -f tests/docker-compose.yml up -d weaviate
until curl -sf http://localhost:9000/v1/.well-known/ready >/dev/null && nc -z localhost 50051; do sleep 2; done
lsof -nP -iTCP:8085 -sTCP:LISTEN
make dev PORT=8085 APP_DIR=$(pwd)/tests/integrations/python
make run-provider-harness-test PROVIDER=anthropic FEATURE="deferred web search" BASE_URL=http://localhost:8085
```

### Cost on the request flow

`BenchmarkWebSearchRequestRoundTrip` (added), `-benchmem`, n=10 per side, darwin/arm64:

| Case | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| Finished search (common case) | 6.869µs, 19.02Ki B/op, 98 allocs/op | 6.850µs, 18.99Ki B/op, 98 allocs/op |
| Pending search | 7.744µs, 21.10Ki B/op, 103 allocs/op | 7.167µs, 19.11Ki B/op, 100 allocs/op |

A finished search adds no allocations: the status is flipped in place on the pointer allocated for that item, and egress adds one string compare. A request with no web search runs none of this code. Nothing is retained past the request.

## Screenshots/Recordings

Not applicable.

## Breaking changes

- [ ] Yes
- [x] No

## Related issues

Closes #9591. Related: #9542.

## Security considerations

None. No change to auth, secrets or what is logged.

- [x] I added/updated tests where appropriate

items.title: [fix]: chat completions - replay thinking content blocks as reasoning details (#8954)
items.body:
## Summary

When Claude thinks before a tool call, the response includes that thinking with a signature. The client has to send it back unchanged on the next request so the model can continue from it. LiteLLM-based clients, including the OpenAI Agents SDK, send it back as a `thinking` item in the assistant message's `content` list.

Bifrost's chat completions endpoint didn't recognize that item. Requests to Bedrock failed with a 500 and requests to Anthropic dropped the thinking without an error.

This PR converts those items to `reasoning_details` when the request is read. Bifrost already sends `reasoning_details` back to Anthropic and Bedrock as signed thinking.

## Changes

- Assistant `thinking` and `redacted_thinking` content blocks become `reasoning_details` entries when a chat request is parsed. Explicit `reasoning_details` take precedence.
- This runs on `/v1/chat/completions` and on the `/openai` and `/litellm` drop-ins. Provider converters are unchanged.
- `/v1/responses` and `/anthropic/v1/messages` are not affected because they already have their own reasoning shapes.

## Type of change

- [x] Bug fix

## Affected areas

- [x] Core (Go)
- [x] Providers/Integrations

## How to test

```sh
cd core && go test ./schemas/... ./providers/...
make run-provider-harness-test PROVIDER=bedrock FEATURE="thinking content block replay" BASE_URL=http://localhost:<port>
```

Unit tests cover the schema, the `/openai` ingress and the Bedrock and Anthropic converters. Harness folder 270 replays a signed thinking block on both chat routes and checks that Converse receives it as `reasoningContent` with the same signature.

## Breaking changes

- [x] No

## Related issues

Closes #8954

items.title: [fix]: vLLM provider - replay assistant reasoning with the canonical field
items.body:
## Summary

Replaying assistant reasoning through built-in vLLM Chat Completions currently sends `reasoning_content`. vLLM versions whose chat parser reads only `reasoning`, including the sampled [v0.21.0 parser](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/v0.21.0/vllm/entrypoints/chat_utils.py), lose that reasoning on the next turn. This change sends the canonical field on typed unary and streaming requests.

AI assistance: Codex was used to implement and review this change.

## Changes

- Reuse the existing Groq/Cerebras assistant alias conversion for built-in vLLM.
- Add neutral-message decoding and mock HTTP regressions for both input spellings, canonical precedence, unary/SSE output and caller immutability. Preserve raw-body/large-payload passthrough and explicit `messages` overrides.
- Add two provider-harness cases that inspect the captured outbound request, plus a provider note and core changelog entry.

vLLM v0.11.1 reads both spellings; v0.22.0 normalizes the legacy spelling. These sampled source contracts support using `reasoning`; they do not establish an exhaustive affected-version range. Generic OpenAI/custom-provider configurations and the Anthropic-compatible endpoint are outside this change.

## Type of change

- [x] Bug fix
- [ ] Feature
- [ ] Refactor
- [ ] Documentation
- [ ] Chore/CI

## Affected areas

- [x] Core (Go)
- [ ] Transports (HTTP)
- [x] Providers/Integrations
- [ ] Plugins

## How to test

Local Go 1.27.0, Windows/amd64, CGO disabled: the original pre-fix run had 7 regression test leaves fail for the expected reasoning-field mismatch and 10 controls pass. After the fix, the focused 23 test leaves and the following broader 102 test leaves passed, with no failures or skips. Both scopes and vet were rerun on the updated branch and passed with the same counts.

```sh
cd core
go test -count=1 -timeout=90s -run '^(TestToOpenAIChatRequest.*|TestConvertBifrostMessagesToOpenAIMessages.*|TestOpenAIChatMessage.*|TestChatCompletion.*|TestResponsesStream_.*)$' ./providers/openai ./providers/vllm

```

The collection passed `augment-provider-harness.mjs` and `filter-collection.mjs --provider vllm --feature vllm-reasoning-replay`, selecting both new cases. Script syntax and synthetic canonical/legacy/missing-body/HTTP-500 controls were checked. No live vLLM, full gateway replay, Linux/race run or complete project CI was executed. GNU make is unavailable on this host.

For live validation, first configure a `vllm` key with `Qwen/Qwen3-0.6B` (or a matching model alias), `use_anthropic_endpoints=false`, and a reachable backend in the selected app profile. Port 8187 must be free or belong to a Bifrost started from this checkout. Run the harness in a second terminal after starting Bifrost; the live run is user-run:

```sh
docker compose -f tests/docker-compose.yml up -d weaviate
until curl -sf http://localhost:9000/v1/.well-known/ready >/dev/null && nc -z localhost 50051; do sleep 2; done
lsof -nP -iTCP:8187 -sTCP:LISTEN
make dev PORT=8187 APP_DIR=$(pwd)/tests/integrations/python
# In a second terminal, from the same checkout:
until curl -sf http://localhost:8187/health >/dev/null; do sleep 2; done
make run-provider-harness-test PROVIDER=vllm FEATURE="vllm-reasoning-replay" BASE_URL=http://localhost:8187 PARALLEL=0 COMPAT=off SKIP_STREAM_CANCEL=1
```

No new configuration fields or environment variables are added.

items.title: [fix]: Gemini provider - replay extra_content.google.thought_signature instead of the skip sentinel
items.body:
## Summary

When a chat request with tool-call history goes to the native `gemini` provider, `convertBifrostMessagesToGemini` recovers a replayed function call's thought signature only from the `<call_id>_ts_<base64url>` id suffix and from `reasoning_details`. Anything else gets `skip_thought_signature_validator`. `ChatAssistantMessageToolCall.ExtraContent` carries `extra_content.google.thought_signature`, the field Google's own OpenAI-compatible endpoint uses, but the Gemini request converter never reads it. A client that does the right thing and sends the signature back as `extra_content` therefore gets its real signature replaced by the sentinel (case P1 of #8149).

## Changes

- `core/providers/gemini/utils.go`: new `thoughtSignatureFromExtraContent`, which reads `google.thought_signature` (base64) from the tool call's `extra_content`. It is tried after the id suffix and `reasoning_details`, and before the sentinel, so requests that already carried a signature behave as before, and requests with neither still get the sentinel.
- `core/providers/gemini/thoughtsignatureextracontent_test.go`: tests and benchmark (below).
- `core/changelog.md`: entry added.

Not changed: the sentinel for history without any signature (P3, P4, P5, P7 in the issue), the Responses converter (`responses.go`, whose tool messages have no `extra_content`), and the Anthropic and genai inbound paths (P5, P6). Those need design decisions the issue leaves open.

## Type of change

- [x] Bug fix

## Affected areas

- [x] Core (Go)
- [x] Providers/Integrations

## How to test

```sh
cd core
go test ./providers/gemini/ -run 'ExtraContentThoughtSignature|NoSignatureStillGetsTheSentinel|UnusableExtraContent' -count=1
go test ./providers/gemini/ -count=1
go test ./providers/gemini/ -run '^$' -bench ExtraContentThoughtSignature -benchmem -count=3
```

`TestConvertBifrostMessagesToGemini_ExtraContentThoughtSignatureIsReplayed` (new) replays the issue's P1 request and expects the decoded signature in the outgoing function-call part. It fails on `dev` (the sentinel is written) and passes now. Two more cases check that history without a signature still gets the sentinel, and that unusable `extra_content` (no `thought_signature`, invalid base64, a different top-level key) falls back to it. The whole `providers/gemini` package passes and `go vet` is clean. The Go tests ran on golang:1.26 with the `go` directive of a temporary module file lowered to 1.26, since `go.mod` asks for 1.27.2.

Benchmark (`BenchmarkConvertBifrostMessagesToGemini_ExtraContentThoughtSignature`, a three-message history with one tool call carrying the field, `-count=3`):

| | ns/op | B/op | allocs/op |
|---|---|---|---|
| dev | 1359 – 1414 | 1732 – 1739 | 24 |
| this PR | 1593 – 1661 | 1785 – 1790 | 25 |

The extra allocation is the decoded signature, which is the work the request needs and which `dev` skipped by writing the sentinel. Calls without `extra_content` return before any parsing.

## Breaking changes

- [x] No

## Related issues

Refs #8149 (fixes its P1 case only, so the issue stays open for the rest).

## Security considerations

None.

## Checklist

- [x] I read `docs/contributing/README.md` and followed the guidelines
- [x] I added/updated tests where appropriate
- [ ] I updated documentation where needed (n/a)
- [x] I verified builds succeed (Go and UI) (Go only; no UI change)
- [ ] I verified the CI pipeline passes locally if applicable

This change was made with Claude Code; the tests and the benchmark above were run on dev and on this branch.

items.title: [Bug]: DeepSeek /responses multi-turn fails because reasoning_text is not replayed

labels.name: datasheet
labels.description: fix needs a change in the pricing or model parameters datasheet

items.body:
### Prerequisites

- [x] I have searched existing issues and discussions to avoid duplicates
- [x] I checked the current `dev` implementation and the current public model-parameters datasheet

### Description

A client request sent to Bifrost's `/responses` endpoint fails on a DeepSeek thinking model during multi-turn replay with:

```text
The request is invalid: The `reasoning_text` in the thinking mode must be passed back to the API. Please check the request body, required fields, and request format.
```

Deployment/alias configuration:

```text
Deployment name: deepseek-v4.1-flash
Model ID:        deepseek/deepseek-flash
Canonical name:  blank (defaults to Model ID)
Provider:        deepseek
```

DeepSeek's official Responses API documentation describes reasoning items whose `content` contains `reasoning_text` blocks, and states that the Responses API is stateless and the full conversation history must be provided on each request:

- https://api-docs.deepseek.com/guides/responses_api/
- https://api-docs.deepseek.com/api/create-response

The current public Bifrost model-parameters row for `deepseek/deepseek-flash` advertises `/v1/responses` and has `supports_reasoning: true`, but does not define:

```json
"supports_reasoning_content_blocks": true
```

Current datasheet:

- https://getbifrost.ai/datasheet/model-parameters

This may cause `ToOpenAIResponsesRequest` to use the name-based fallback, which currently returns true only when the model name contains `gpt-oss`. When false, reasoning content can be removed or a reasoning-only input item can be skipped.

However, the native DeepSeek provider's current `Responses` implementation normally converts the request through `request.ToChatRequest()` and calls `ChatCompletion`. Therefore the actual defect may instead be in the Responses → Chat replay path, where `reasoning_text` should become `reasoning_content`, or it may depend on the selected provider/endpoint path.

Could you confirm which path should handle native DeepSeek `/responses` requests and ensure the returned reasoning state is preserved on the next turn?

Related issues/PRs:

- #6111 (`reasoning_content` missing in DeepSeek thinking mode)
- #5887 (DeepSeek thinking lost in multi-turn OpenAI-compatible requests)
- #3584 (preserve reasoning while converting Responses to Chat)

### Steps to reproduce

1. Configure the DeepSeek provider with an alias/deployment:

   ```json
   {
     "deepseek-v4.1-flash": {
       "model_id": "deepseek/deepseek-flash"
     }
   }
   ```

2. Send a thinking-enabled request to Bifrost's `/responses` endpoint using `deepseek-v4.1-flash`.
3. Continue the conversation and replay the previous response output/history, including its reasoning item.
4. Observe the upstream validation error saying that `reasoning_text` must be passed back.

A useful diagnostic is to compare the inbound Responses payload with the upstream raw request and verify whether the reasoning item is dropped or translated without its text.

### Expected behavior

Bifrost preserves the DeepSeek reasoning item across `/responses` turns, or converts its `reasoning_text` to `reasoning_content` when the native DeepSeek implementation falls back to Chat Completions.

### Actual behavior

A subsequent `/responses` turn is rejected because the required `reasoning_text` is not passed back.

### Affected area(s)

Core (Go), Framework/model datasheet

### Version

Current `dev` behavior/source inspected on 2026-09-18; exact deployed release version not yet confirmed.

### Environment

```text
Inbound endpoint: /responses
Provider: deepseek
Deployment name: deepseek-v4.1-flash
Model ID: deepseek/deepseek-flash
Canonical model name: blank
```

### Relevant logs/output

```shell
The request is invalid: The `reasoning_text` in the thinking mode must be passed back to the API. Please check the request body, required fields, and request format.
```

### Regression?

Unknown.

### Severity

Medium (some functionality impaired)

items.title: [fix]: fold replayed reasoning_details into assistant reasoning on native chat ingress
items.body:
## What

Replays of assistant reasoning arriving as `reasoning_details[].text` on the **native** `/v1/chat/completions` surface were silently dropped before reaching the model. Supersedes #6645, which went stale after `#7318` rewrote this function; issue #5274 remains open.

## The bug

`/openai/*` normalizes replayed reasoning across three spellings (`ConvertOpenAIMessagesToBifrostMessages`, dd927388d). The native surface parses the body straight into `schemas.ChatMessage`, so that converter never runs — and `ChatAssistantMessage.UnmarshalJSON` folded `reasoning_content` alone. A caller replaying `reasoning_details[].text` (OpenRouter's documented spelling, and exactly what a client that captured Bifrost's own response emits next turn) kept `Reasoning` nil.

Silent, because nothing errors: `ConvertBifrostMessagesToOpenAIMessages` carries reasoning to an OpenAI-compatible upstream only as `reasoning_content` — `reasoning_details` is inbound-only there by design — so the chain of thought never reached the model. Multi-turn tool loops ran with no prior thinking block, and the model began confabulating (inventing tool results, skipping cases outright).

## Change

`firstNonEmptyReplayedReasoning` applied in `ChatAssistantMessage.UnmarshalJSON` and `ChatStreamResponseChoiceDelta.UnmarshalJSON`, at the precedence the `/openai/*` surface already uses: **`reasoning_content` > `reasoning` > first non-empty `reasoning.text` detail**. Both entry surfaces agreeing on which spelling wins is the point; otherwise the same body means different things depending on the path it arrived on.

Two rules are load-bearing on top of #7318:

- **Empty is absent, never a value.** An unconditional `reasoning_content` assignment (what #6645 did) writes `""` over a real reasoning text on a DeepSeek content-phase frame, after which #7318's emptiness check nulls it — reintroducing #7294 from the other side. `{reasoning:"real", reasoning_content:""}` now keeps `"real"`.
- **A detail qualifies on its `Type`, not merely on having a text field.** `reasoning.encrypted` / `reasoning.summary` / `reasoning.content_blocks` carry opaque bytes or a derived digest, so plaintext stuffed into one must not be forwarded as `reasoning_content`. Bifrost always stamps `type` when it synthesizes a detail, so a client replaying our own response is unaffected.

Structured details are read, never consumed, pruned or reordered — Anthropic, Gemini and Bedrock signed replay reads `ReasoningDetails` directly and must keep seeing exactly what the client sent.

The helper is exported and `openai.ConvertOpenAIMessagesToBifrostMessages` (the `/openai/*` ingress) calls it rather than keeping its own copy, which had drifted in two ways: it checked only for nil, so `{"reasoning_content":"","reasoning":"B"}` selected `""` and then failed the DeepSeek replay gate; and it never checked `detail.Type`, so text on a `reasoning.encrypted`, `reasoning.summary` or untyped detail reached the upstream as `reasoning_content`. One rule set, asserted on both surfaces by `TestInboundReasoningSpellingsAgreeOnEmptyAndOpaque`.

## Tests

Red before green. The fold cases fail on `dev` before the change (`TestChatAssistantMessageIngressFoldsReasoningDetails`, `...ReasoningDetailsEdgeCases`, and six in `reasoningroundtrip_test.go`), pass after — including the three cases pinning the type guard. `core/schemas` and `core/providers/openai` green; `gofmt`/`go vet` clean.

Harness pin as **folder 128** of `provider-harness.json` (4 rows). DeepSeek carries it because its endpoint forces `thinking:disabled` only when an assistant tool_call turn carries no replayable reasoning, so whether the replay survived is visible from the response alone — without `allow_per_request_raw_override`, which defaults false in the harness deployment. The encrypted and empty-detail rows are controls proving the fold reads plaintext only. The OpenAI row asserts `extra_fields.raw_request.messages[].reasoning_content` directly and skips where capture is unavailable. Validated structurally:

```
node tests/e2e/api/runners/augment-provider-harness.mjs --source tests/e2e/api/collections/provider-harness.json --out tmp/harness-augmented.json
node tests/e2e/api/runners/filter-collection.mjs --source tmp/harness-augmented.json --out tmp/filtered.json --feature "reasoning_details"
```

## Not related to this change

`TestRealtimeWebRTCUpstreamErrorCarriesRetryHint` fails 3/3 on pristine `dev` independently of this PR (`realtime_test.go:853: StatusCode = 0x3dd355c1d878, want 502` — a pointer where an int is expected). Reported here so a red provider run is not read as caused by this change; happy to file it separately.

items.title: [Bug]: /anthropic/v1/messages drops the web_search_tool_result of a resumed (deferred) search, on responses and on replay
items.body:
### Prerequisites

- [x] I have searched existing issues and discussions to avoid duplicates
- [x] I am using the latest version (or have tested against main/nightly)

### Description

When Anthropic resumes a deferred `web_search`, it returns the search result at the **start of the next assistant message**: a `web_search_tool_result` whose `server_tool_use` was in the previous assistant message. Bifrost drops that block everywhere:

- **Non-streaming response:** the client gets the text but not the `web_search_tool_result`.
- **Streaming response:** the block is skipped (`ToBifrostResponsesStream` returns nothing for a result whose `tool_use_id` is not the active search: "If no matching tool ID, skip").
- **Request replay:** `attachWebSearchSourcesToCall` only looks for the call inside the same message, so a replayed result in a later message is dropped.

The cause is the same in all three: a `web_search_call` in the neutral schema carries the call and its result together, so there is no way to represent a result whose call is in an earlier turn.

Background on deferral: Anthropic defers a search called in the same turn as a client tool. The turn ends with a bare `server_tool_use`; the client sends it back with the client `tool_result` blocks; Anthropic runs the search and puts the result at the start of its next message. #9591 / #9630 fix the request side of the continuation.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Non-streaming response from Anthropic for the continuation:

```json
{"role":"assistant","stop_reason":"end_turn","content":[
  {"type":"web_search_tool_result","tool_use_id":"srvtoolu_B","content":[{"type":"web_search_result","url":"https://k8s.io","title":"K8s","encrypted_content":"enc"}]},
  {"type":"text","text":"OOMKilled"}]}
```

`ToBifrostResponsesResponse` then `ToAnthropicResponsesResponse` returns `content: [text]`.

2. The same message streamed (`content_block_start` for the `web_search_tool_result`, `content_block_stop`, then text): the client receives only the text block.

3. Replay of the full conversation on the next request:

```
user, assistant[tool_use, server_tool_use(srvtoolu_B)], user[tool_result], assistant[web_search_tool_result(srvtoolu_B), text], user
```

What Bifrost sends upstream:

- `transports/v2.5.0`: `assistant[tool_use, server_tool_use, web_search_tool_result(empty)]`, `user[tool_result]`, `assistant[text]`. The real result is dropped and an empty one is made up after the client `tool_use`, which is the #9591 400.
- With #9630 applied: `assistant[tool_use, server_tool_use]`, `user[tool_result]`, `assistant[text]`. The real result is dropped and the `server_tool_use` in the earlier turn has no result anywhere.

### Expected behavior

The `web_search_tool_result` is passed through in the message where Anthropic put it, on the response (streaming and non-streaming) and on replay, without adding another `server_tool_use` for it.

### Actual behavior

The block is dropped on all three paths. The client never sees the search sources for that call, and a conversation that keeps going replays a search with no result.

### Suggested fix

A neutral item for a result whose call is in an earlier message. For example, a `web_search_call` item that carries only the call id and sources with a marker (or a dedicated item type), which the Anthropic egress renders as a lone `web_search_tool_result` block in the current message, and which the ingress emits when a `web_search_tool_result` has no matching call in the same message. The same gap probably exists for `web_fetch_tool_result` and the other server tools that Anthropic can defer, which use the same attach-to-call pattern.

### Affected area(s)

Anthropic provider, `/anthropic/v1/messages` streaming, non-streaming and request conversion (`core/providers/anthropic/responses.go`, `utils.go` `attachWebSearchSourcesToCall`)

### Version

transports/v2.5.0 and `dev`. Also checked v2.4.0.

### Environment

Self-hosted Bifrost (Kubernetes, linux/amd64), Anthropic provider with API keys, clients speaking the Anthropic Messages API.

### Regression?

No.

### Severity

Medium: the run continues because the model saw the results server-side, but the client loses the search results of every deferred search, and later replays carry a search with no result.

Related: #9591, #9630, #9542.

items.title: fix(semanticcache): don't cache or replay raw payloads stripped from the client
items.body:
## Summary

With `store_raw_request_response` on and `send_back_raw_request` / `send_back_raw_response` off, core keeps the raw provider payloads for logging and drops them from the response it hands to the client. That strip happens in `tryRequest` after the post-hook chain returns.

Since #7304 the semantic cache serializes the response inside `PostLLMHook`, which is before that strip. So the cache entry ends up with `raw_request` / `raw_response` in `extra_fields`, and the next hit replays them as part of the short-circuit response. A client that should never see the upstream payloads gets them, and it can be a different caller from the one whose request produced them.

## Changes

Raw payloads describe the upstream call made for the request that wrote the entry. A hit makes no upstream call, so they never belong in a replay. The hitting request's own send-back policy is also not known when the hit is served: core derives the drop flags per attempt in the request worker (`applyRawCaptureSignals`), after the pre-hooks have run, so a hit served from `PreLLMHook` always sees them unset.

- `PostLLMHook`: remove `raw_request` / `raw_response` from the serialized bytes before they go to the writer. This covers both the single-response write and the per-chunk stream accumulator, since both use the same bytes. The live response isn't touched, so core's strip and the logging plugins behave as before.
- Cache hits (non-stream and stream): clear both fields on the replayed response, so entries written before this change don't leak them either.
- A request that asks for raw payloads back still gets them on a miss. On a hit it gets none, since no upstream call was made for it.

## Type of change

- [x] Bug fix
- [ ] Feature
- [ ] Refactor
- [ ] Documentation
- [ ] Chore/CI

## Affected areas

- [ ] Core (Go)
- [ ] Transports (HTTP)
- [ ] Providers/Integrations
- [x] Plugins
- [ ] UI (React)
- [ ] Docs

## How to test

```sh
cd plugins/semanticcache
go test -race -count=1 ./...
```

`plugin_raw_fields_test.go` has five tests. Against current `dev`, four fail (raw fields in the stored entry, in cached stream chunks, and on both replay paths) and one passes (live response untouched). With the fix all five pass. The two ownership tests from #7233 used `raw_response` as their marker for a mutation made after the hook returns; they now mutate the response content instead, and still fail if the writer serializes after the hook returns. The whole module passes under `-race`.
